summary: Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Petersburg University under Ivan Minayev (~1881–1885). He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, the Russian Academy of Sciences (1904–1929), the Asiatic Museum, and the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Serinity Young was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and Vidya Dehejia. In 2000, she held posts at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University.

Seung-yeon Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Lee completed doctoral studies under Sang-hae Lee and held posts at the Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation and Sungkyunkwan University.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Seoul National University and earned a PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. in 2011. Koh was appointed as a researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seán McLoughlin is a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Manchester. He served as Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds (attested 2005).

Shailendra Bhandare is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He held positions at the Fitzwilliam Museum, the British Museum, the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022), and served as a Fellow at St Cross College, Oxford (attested 2022).
Shan Shan Zhao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with teachers Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.
Shane McCausland is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at Princeton University from 1996 to 2000. He held a post at SOAS University of London in 2009.
Shanshan Jia is an Indologist who pursued doctoral studies in Indology at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Harunaga Isaacson (attested 2015).

Shaoyong Ye is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University under Qing Duan by 2009 and served there as an associate professor (attested 2010–2016).
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under the doctoral supervision of Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).
Sharon Salzberg is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at the University at Buffalo (~1969–1973) and with traditional teacher Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Scottish Church College (~1928–1932) and the University of Calcutta (~1937), where he later served as a lecturer (~1945–1964).

Shayne Clarke is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Bukkyo University, the University of Canterbury (MA), and UCLA (PhD, 2006 under Gregory Schopen). He later served as associate professor at McMaster University (attested 2015–2016).
Shek-wing Tam was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche (~1970–1987). He held a post at Renmin University of China (~2007).

Sheldon Pollock is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard (~1971–1975). He held posts at the University of Iowa (~1976–1989), the University of Chicago (~1989–2001), Columbia University (~2001), and the Clay Sanskrit Library (~2005–2008).

Sheng Yen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Dongchu (~1959–1977) and earned a doctorate at Rissho University (~1969–1975). He held posts at National Cheng Kung University and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1985–2009).

Shenghai Li is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under doctoral supervisor Donald R. Davis Jr., studying also with Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Ram Shankar Tripathi, and multiple traditional teachers.

Shenpen Hookham is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under several traditional teachers and completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (~1979–1986) supervised by Michael M. Broido.
Shi Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007). He held posts at the University of Hong Kong and as a professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2013).
